scope_items.item: iam_policy_validate: is_principal=True (default) leaves IsPrincipal out of the request
Return validation as today plus evaluation (Allow/Deny as is) when <Evaluation> is present
Docstring, docs/tools/iam_policy_bindings.md and regenerated docs/tools.md describe measured behaviour
rest.iam_query: malformed 2xx body parsed from <{action}Response> element, else ToolRefused naming the action
Errors append <Detail> as {Code}: {Message} ({Detail}) in _xml_error and 2xx <Error> branch; unchanged without Detail
Tool tests: default omits IsPrincipal, is_principal=False sends false, set(form) updated
Tool tests: malformed 200 without Evaluation, with Allow/Deny, 400 MalformedPolicyDocument with Detail, 400 Missing Principal, unparseable 200
tests/test_rest.py: iam_query fallback and <Detail> in error text
Live test: default lint succeeds, evaluated call asserts evaluation == Allow, syntax-error policy raises MalformedPolicyDocument
.dmx/techContext.md: replace 'still open' ValidatePolicy note with confirmed behaviour

edge_cases.description: Well-formed IAM bodies (GetUserMFA, existing tests) take the unchanged parse path
2xx body with no <{action}Response> element, empty body, or mismatched tags raises ToolRefused instead of ParseError
Error without <Detail> or with whitespace-only Detail keeps the original message
Empty <Evaluation> element is not added as evaluation
Explicit is_principal=True behaves like the default (IsPrincipal omitted)
2xx <Error> inside a malformed body is still raised after fallback parsing
